rule_metadata.description: The concealment of a non-vowelled Noon (نْ) or Tanween when followed by any of the 15 remaining Ikhfa letters, pronounced between Izhar and Idgham with a 2-count nasal Ghunnah.

theoretical_foundation.linguistic_definition: Ikhfa literally means concealment or hiding (السِّتْر).
theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: When a non-vowelled Noon (نْ) or Tanween is followed by any of the 15 specific Ikhfa letters across two words (or within a single word), the Noon is neither pronounced fully clear nor merged completely. Instead, it is concealed while holding a 2-count nasal Ghunnah from the nasal cavity (Khayshum), and the tongue hovers near the articulation point of the succeeding letter.
theoretical_foundation.mnemonic_poetry_reference: Found in the famous line: صِفْ ذَا ثَنَا كَمْ جَادَ شَخْصٌ قَدْ سَمَا ... دُمْ طَيِّبًا زِدْ فِى تُقًى ضَِعْ ظَالِمَا (the first letter of each word represents an Ikhfa letter).
theoretical_foundation.acoustic_rule: The nasal Ghunnah duration is exactly 2 counts. Crucially, the quality of the Ghunnah adapts to the upcoming letter: it becomes heavy (Tafkhim) when followed by heavy letters (ص, ض, ط, ظ, ق), and light (Tarqeeq) when followed by light letters.
theoretical_foundation.mushaf_indicator: The Noon Sakinah has no Sukoon sign, and the succeeding letter does NOT have a Tashdeed (distinguishing it from Idgham).

practical_examples.breakdown: Light Ikhfa: Tongue hovers near the edge of upper teeth while holding 2-count nasal hum.
Heavy Ikhfa (Tafkhim): Because Sad (ص) is a heavy letter, the nasal Ghunnah must be pronounced with an elevated, heavy back of the tongue.
Single-word Ikhfa occurring between Noon and Ta inside the same word.
Tanween followed by Seen; light concealment with tongue behind lower front teeth.

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the complete mechanics of Ikhfa Haqiqi:
options: Encounter Noon Sakinah/Tanween + 1 of 15 Ikhfa letters -> conceal Noon sound between Izhar and Idgham -> hold 2-count nasal Ghunnah (heavy for heavy letters, light for light letters) -> transition smoothly into next letter without Shaddah
Read clear Noon -> pause -> read next letter
